text:
Aaron Ekblad scored his first goal of the season on Nov. 2, short-handed against Detroit. It took until November. That's a slow start for a former first overall pick and Calder winner with two Cups, and his 5 points in 16 games won't change many minds.

The underlying numbers should. Florida takes almost 63% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Ekblad on the ice at five on five, more than 16 points better than without him. That's an enormous gap, and the Panthers have scored 8.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, a big number for a defenseman. His pairing with Gustav Forsling has taken 63% of the expected goals while being outscored 14-8. That won't last.

There's a counterweight. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with opponents getting more chances with him on (bottom 7%). So either this season's on-ice numbers are the real Ekblad or last year's were, and 16 games is the smaller sample. He's 30, playing 21 minutes a night, and the minutes haven't moved. We project about 27 points. When the goals start going in for his pair, they'll go in quickly.
headline: Ekblad's numbers are better than his luck
